about: ZIP to utility, permit office, interconnection path, and days to a first home-battery install. Every figure is sourced or the word unknown.

coverage.note: Texas first, plus Illinois, Georgia, and Connecticut. Austin, Houston, Dallas, and San Antonio ZCTAs are in the file. The city or county comes from the 2020 Census overlap. The wires utility comes from the NREL/OpenEI 2024 ZIP file when that file names one. Oncor, CenterPoint, AEP Texas, and TNMP are not in that file, so for Texas the wires companies inside retail choice come from Power to Choose, the PUCT's plan site, ZIP by ZIP (retrieved 2026-11-04). A ZIP split between a retail-choice wires company and a city utility or co-op lists both. A ZCTA is not a USPS ZIP code.
gaps: Rows whose OpenEI ownership is Retail Power Marketer (TXU Energy and Reliant among them) are not treated as the wires utility. A ZIP that lists only a marketer has utility unknown.
Crew days are unknown. No construction duration was added.
ZCTAs follow ZIP codes as of January 1, 2020. A ZIP created after that, a PO Box-only ZIP, or a code with no ZCTA is not covered.

TX: OpenEI 2024 ZIP rows for Texas do not include Oncor, CenterPoint, AEP Texas, TNMP. The 2022 vintage was scanned the same way and is also missing Oncor, CenterPoint, AEP Texas, TNMP. The Texas wires utility inside retail choice comes from Power to Choose (PUCT) instead: 1257 of 1989 Texas ZCTAs list retail plans over at least one wires company.

Power to Choose answers by ZIP, not by address. It lists plans if any part of the ZIP is inside retail choice, so a ZIP split between a retail-choice wires company and a city utility or co-op (Denton 76201 is one) shows both, and the bill decides. County-level EIA-861 data was not used to assign utilities: 540 Texas ZCTAs sit in a county that EIA-861 2024 lists with more than one investor-owned wires company (Dallas County has Oncor and TNMP), so a county answer would be a guess. 21 ZIP and wires-company pairs from Power to Choose are not in EIA-861 for the ZIP's main county. 8 of those are in another county the ZIP touches. 13 are in no county the ZIP touches (75153 AEP Texas North, 76020 AEP Texas North, 76301 Texas-New Mexico Power (TNMP), 78734 AEP Texas North, 78832 AEP Texas North, 78851 AEP Texas Central, 78956 AEP Texas Central, 79079 AEP Texas North, 79097 Oncor Electric Delivery, 79124 Oncor Electric Delivery, 79237 AEP Texas North, 79240 AEP Texas North, 79250 AEP Texas North); they are kept as Power to Choose lists them, and the bill decides.
Power to Choose returned an error for no Texas ZCTA. Those ZIPs show the retail-choice check as unknown.
The CenterPoint distributed-generation FAQ at https://www.centerpointenergy.com/en-us/Services/Pages/DGAP-FAQs.aspx returned HTTP 404 on 2026-11-03, so no CenterPoint-specific day count is stored.

No published city permit-review duration, in days, is on file for Austin, Houston, Dallas, or San Antonio. Houston is on the SolarAPP+ list for solar PV and not for solar plus storage. That list does not state a day count.

PUCT 25.211(m) is an outside limit (four weeks for pre-certified equipment, six weeks otherwise). The rule text says cooperatives are covered only by subsection (o). The limit is not applied to municipal utilities or cooperatives, and it is not used as a typical duration.
IL: No interconnection clock and no permit-review duration in days is on file for Illinois utilities or permit offices. The interconnection path for an investor-owned utility here is unknown in this file, and the day total stays unknown.
The Power to Choose retail-choice check is Texas only. Whether a Illinois home buys power from a retail supplier is not in this file.

OpenEI lists some utilities here twice, once with Bundled and once with Delivery customers (homes that buy power from a retail supplier). Those rows are merged into one utility per EIA number, with service type Bundled and Delivery.
GA: No interconnection clock and no permit-review duration in days is on file for Georgia utilities or permit offices. The interconnection path for an investor-owned utility here is unknown in this file, and the day total stays unknown.
The Power to Choose retail-choice check is Texas only. Whether a Georgia home buys power from a retail supplier is not in this file.
CT: No interconnection clock and no permit-review duration in days is on file for Connecticut utilities or permit offices. The interconnection path for an investor-owned utility here is unknown in this file, and the day total stays unknown.
The Power to Choose retail-choice check is Texas only. Whether a Connecticut home buys power from a retail supplier is not in this file.

explainer: Type the ZIP on the electric bill. The utility is whoever the public ZIP file names as the wires company, plus, in Texas, any wires company Power to Choose sells retail plans over in that ZIP. The permit office is the incorporated city or town that covers at least half of this ZIP's census land, and otherwise the county. The day count adds three clocks: permit review, interconnection, and the crew. If any of those is not a published calendar-day number, the total stays unknown. A business-day window, or a rule that says within four weeks, is shown beside the formula and is not turned into a single number.

formula.rule: Add the three inputs only when each one is a single calendar-day number. An outside limit (within four weeks) is not that number. A business-day window is not converted into calendar days. If any input is missing, days_to_first_install is unknown.

ahj_rule.text: This site's rule, not a Census rule: the permitting authority is the incorporated place (class code starting with C) with the largest land overlap when that overlap is at least half of the ZCTA. Otherwise it is the county with the largest land overlap. A ZIP can cross city lines. Confirm with the city before applying.

ptc.title: Power to Choose (Public Utility Commission of Texas), retail plans by ZIP
ptc.quote: One request per Texas ZCTA to the PUCT Web API. Each plan carries company_tdu_name, the wires company the plan is delivered over. No plans means no retail choice in that ZIP. Plan prices were not copied.

eia861-2024-territory.title: EIA-861 2024, Service_Territory (utilities by county)
eia861-2024-territory.quote: Utility number, name, state, and county for each county a utility serves. Used to confirm EIA numbers and to check the Power to Choose answer, not to assign a utility to a ZIP.

puct-55999-lpl.title: ERCOT notification regarding the upcoming transition of LP&L's customers to retail competition, PUCT Project 55999, item 15
puct-55999-lpl.quote: Customers of the City of Lubbock, acting by and through Lubbock Power & Light, (LP&L) will begin transitioning to competitive Retail Electric Providers (REPs) on or about March 4, 2024. Customers will be transitioned to REPs based on LP&L's meter-read cycles, with the transition scheduled to be completed on or about April 1, 2024.

openei-2024.title: NREL/OpenEI, U.S. Electric Utility Companies and Rates: Look-up by Zip Code (2024)
openei-2024.quote: Compiled by NREL from ABB Velocity Suite and EIA-861. Average residential, commercial, and industrial rates with likely ZIP codes, for investor-owned and non-investor-owned utilities. Rates in the file are utility averages, not ZIP averages, and are not copied into this file.

census-zcta-county.title: Census Bureau, 2020 ZCTA to County Relationship File
census-zcta-county.quote: Each record is one intersection of a 2020 ZIP Code Tabulation Area and a 2020 county. ZCTAs follow ZIP codes as of January 1, 2020. They are not the USPS ZIP list.

census-zcta-place.title: Census Bureau, 2020 ZCTA to Place Relationship File
census-zcta-place.quote: Each record is one intersection of a 2020 ZCTA and a 2020 place. Incorporated places use class codes that start with C. Census designated places are not treated as the permit office.

solarapp.title: SolarAPP+ participating jurisdictions CSV
solarapp.quote: The public where-available page links this CSV. Column 6 is published with the header #e0e0e4 and TRUE/FALSE values; this file stores that column as pv. Solar + Storage is the published battery column. Jurisdictions outside TX, IL, GA, and CT were not committed.

puct-25211.title: PUCT Substantive Rule 25.211, Interconnection of On-Site Distributed Generation
puct-25211.quote: Effective 1/5/17. Applies to an electric utility. The only part that applies to electric cooperatives is subsection (o). Subsection (m): pre-certified equipment within four weeks of a completed application; other facilities within six weeks.

puct-ercot-tdus.title: PUCT, Guide to the Electric Rate Case Process for Investor-owned Utilities inside ERCOT
puct-ercot-tdus.quote: CenterPoint Energy, Oncor, TNMP, AEP Texas are investor-owned Transmission and Distribution (TDU) electric utilities operating the poles and wires. TDUs charge delivery rates to retail electric providers.

austin-energy-ica.title: Austin Energy, Residential Interconnection Agreement for Solar and Energy Storage Systems
austin-energy-ica.quote: Effective 10/1/2026. Austin Energy will install a solar meter in addition to the existing revenue meter, typically within 5-10 business days of a passed final solar inspection.

pec-interconnection.title: Pedernales Electric Cooperative, Interconnection Process
pec-interconnection.quote: PEC's Energy Services Advisor will receive your request to inspect and perform a site visit within 10-15 business days though we strive for sooner.

oncor-residential.title: Oncor, Residential and small commercial solar
oncor-residential.quote: Oncor does not publish its own turnaround in days. The page says timelines vary and refers readers to PUCT Substantive Rule 25.211 section (m). The page spells the word Substantitive.

clocks.about: Outside limit after a completed application for pre-certified equipment. Not a typical duration. The rule applies to an electric utility. It says cooperatives are covered only by subsection (o), so this clock is not applied to cooperatives or to municipal utilities.
clocks.quote: For a facility with pre-certified equipment, interconnection shall take place within four weeks of the utility's receipt of a completed application.

clocks.about: Outside limit for equipment that is not pre-certified, from the same subsection. Not a typical duration, and not applied to cooperatives or municipal utilities.
clocks.quote: For other facilities, interconnection shall take place within six weeks of the utility's receipt of a completed application.

clocks.about: Austin Energy installs a solar meter after a passed final solar inspection. The agreement covers solar and energy storage, but this sentence is the solar-meter step. It is not permit review and not crew time, and it is not added into the calendar-day total.
clocks.quote: Austin Energy will install a solar meter in addition to the existing revenue meter, typically within 5-10 business days of a passed final solar inspection.

clocks.about: How soon PEC says it will visit after the member requests the final inspection. The page does not state how long the application review before installation takes, so that earlier step stays unknown.
clocks.quote: PEC's Energy Services Advisor will receive your request to inspect and perform a site visit within 10-15 business days though we strive for sooner.

clocks.display: no day count of Oncor's own; points at PUCT 25.211(m)
clocks.about: Oncor's residential solar page does not give its own turnaround in days. It points readers at PUCT 25.211(m). Oncor is not in the OpenEI ZIP file; it attaches to a ZIP where Power to Choose lists plans over Oncor.
clocks.quote: There are various timelines to process interconnection applications depending on the generation equipment and if system upgrades are required. For more information, please refer to the PUCT Substantitive Rule 25.211 section (m).

retail_choice.rule: A Texas ZIP's tdus are the wires companies named on the plans Power to Choose lists for that ZIP. A city utility or co-op that appears there is inside retail choice: a retail electric provider sells the power and the utility owns the wires. A city utility or co-op that never appears there statewide is outside retail choice.
